translations.text: In the beginning the Word existed, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
He was with God in the beginning.
Everything came into being through him, and without him nothing that came into being came into being.
Life is in him, and life is the light of humanity.
And the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not grasp it.
There was a man sent from God whose name was John.
He came as a witness, to testify about the light, so that everyone might believe through him.
He was not the light, but he was to testify about the light.
The true light, which gives light to everyone, is coming into the world.
He was in the world, and the world came into being through him, and the world did not recognize him.
He came to what was his own, and his own people did not receive him.
But to those who received him, he gave the authority to become children of God—to those who believe in his name.
These did not come from the will of blood and flesh, nor from human will, but were born from God.
And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we saw his glory, like the glory of an only son from his father, full of grace and truth.
John testifies about him and cries out, saying, “This is the one about whom I said, ‘The one who comes after me has come to be ahead of me, because he existed before me.’”
For from his fullness we have all received life, and grace in place of grace.
For the law was given through Moses, but grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
No one has ever seen God. God, the only Son, who is in his Father's embrace, is the one who has spoken about him.
And this is John's testimony when the Jews sent priests and Levites to him from Jerusalem to ask him, “Who are you?”
And he openly acknowledged it and did not deny it: “I am not the Christ.”
Then they asked him, “Are you Elijah?” And he said, “I am not.” “Are you the prophet?” And he answered, “No.”
They said, “Then who are you, so that we can give an answer to those who sent us? What do you say about yourself?”
He said, “I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness, ‘Make the Lord's path straight,’ just as Isaiah the prophet said.”
And they sent some people to him from among the Pharisees.
They asked him, “Why, then, do you baptize if you are not the Christ, or Elijah, or the prophet?”
John answered them, saying, “I baptize you in water, but among you stands someone whom you do not know,
the one who comes after me, whose sandal strap I am not worthy to untie.”
These things happened in Beth-arabah, on the other side of the Jordan, at the place where John was baptizing.
The next day he saw Jesus coming toward him and said, “Look, the Lamb of God, who will take away the sin of the world!”
“This is the one I spoke about when I said, ‘A man is coming after me who has taken his place ahead of me, because he was before me.’”
“I myself did not know him, but I came baptizing with water so that he might be revealed to Israel.”
And John testified, saying, “I saw the Spirit coming down from heaven like a dove, and it rested on him.”

“I myself did not know him, but the one who sent me to baptize with water said to me, ‘The one on whom you see the Spirit coming down and remaining is the one who will baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire.’”
“And I have seen and testified that this is the chosen Son of God.”
The next day John was again standing there with two of his disciples.
And when he looked at Jesus walking by, he said, “Look, the Christ, the Lamb of God!”
His two disciples heard him speaking and followed Jesus.
When Jesus turned around and saw them following him, he said to them, “What are you looking for?” They said to him, “Rabbi”—which is translated “Teacher”—“where are you staying?”
He said to them, “Come, and you will see.” So they came and saw where he was staying, and they stayed with him that day. It was the tenth hour.
Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, was one of the two who had heard John and followed him.
He first found his brother Simon and said to him, “We have found the Messiah”—which is translated “the Christ.”
And he brought him to Jesus. When Jesus looked at him, he said, “You are Simon, the son of John. You will be called Cephas”—which is translated “Peter.”
The next day he wanted to leave for Galilee, and he found Philip. Jesus said to him, “Follow me.”
Now Philip was from Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter.
Philip found Nathanael and said to him, “We have found the one Moses wrote about in the Law, and the prophets also wrote about: Jesus, the son of Joseph, from Nazareth.”
Nathanael said to him, “Can anything good come from Nazareth?” Philip said to him, “Come and see.”
Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him and said about him, “Look, a true Israelite, in whom there is no deceit!”
Nathanael said to him, “How do you know me?” Jesus answered him, “Before Philip called you, I saw you under the fig tree.”
Nathanael answered him, “Rabbi, you are the Son of God; you are the King of Israel!”
Jesus answered him, “Because I told you that I saw you under the fig tree, you believed. You will see greater things than these.”
And he said to him, “Truly, truly, I tell you all, you will see heaven open and the angels of God going up and coming down upon the Son of Man.”
And on the third day there was a wedding in Cana of Galilee, and Jesus’ mother was there.
Jesus and his disciples were also invited to the wedding.
And when they ran out of wine, Jesus’ mother said to him, “They have no wine.”
Jesus said to her, “Woman, what do you want with me? My hour has not yet come.”
His mother said to those serving, “Do whatever he tells you.”
Now six stone water jars were standing there for the Jewish purification rites, each holding two or three measures.
Jesus said to them, “Fill the jars with water.” And they filled them to the brim.
He said to them, “Now draw some out and take it to the master of the banquet.” And they took it.

When the master of the banquet tasted the water that had become wine, he did not know where it came from. But the servants who had filled the jars with water knew. The master of the banquet called the bridegroom.
He said to him, “Everyone serves the good wine first, and when people have become drunk, they serve the inferior wine. But you have kept the good wine until now.”
This was the first sign Jesus performed in Cana of Galilee. He revealed his glory, and his disciples believed in him.
After this he went down to Capernaum with his mother, his brothers, and his disciples, and they stayed there a few days.
Now the Jewish Passover was approaching, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
In the temple he found people selling cattle and doves, and money changers sitting there.
He made a whip out of cords and drove everyone out of the temple, along with the sheep and cattle. He poured out the money changers’ coins and overturned their tables.
He said to those selling doves, “Take these things out of here! Do not make my Father’s house a marketplace.”
His disciples remembered that it is written, “Zeal for your house will consume me.”
Then the Jews responded to him, “What sign can you show us for doing these things?”
Jesus answered them, “Destroy this temple, and I will raise it up in three days.”
Then the Jews said, “It took forty-six years to build this temple, and you will raise it up in three days?”
But he was speaking about the temple of his body.
So when he rose from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this, and they believed the Scripture and the words Jesus had spoken.
While he was in Jerusalem at the Passover festival, many believed in his name when they saw the signs he was performing.
But Jesus himself did not entrust himself to them, because he knew everyone.
He did not need anyone to testify about human beings, for he himself knew what was in a person.
Now there was a man from among the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a leader of the Jews.
He came to him at night and said to him, “Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher who has come from God, for no one can perform these signs you perform unless God is with him.”
Jesus answered him, “Truly, truly, I tell you, unless someone is born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”
Nicodemus said to him, “How can a person be born again when he is old? Can he enter his mother’s womb again and be born?”
Jesus answered, “Truly, truly, I tell you, unless someone is born of water and Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God.”
What is born of the flesh is flesh, and what is born of the Spirit is spirit.
Do not be surprised that I told you, ‘You must be born again.’
The wind blows where it wants, and you hear its sound, but you do not know where it came from or where it is going. This is how it is with everyone who has been born of the Spirit.
Nicodemus answered him, ‘How can these things happen?’
Jesus answered him, ‘You are the teacher of Israel, and you do not understand these things?’
Truly, truly, I tell you, we speak about what we know and testify about what we see, but you do not accept our testimony.
If I have told you about earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you about heavenly things?
And no one has gone up to heaven except the one who came from heaven, the Son of Man.
And just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up.
So that he may give everyone who believes in him eternal life in him.
For this is how God loved the world: he gave his only Son, so that everyone who believes in him would not perish but would receive eternal life.
For God did not send the Son into the world to judge the world, but so that the world would be saved through him.
The one who believes in him will not be judged. But the one who does not believe has already been judged, because he has not believed in the name of God's only Son.
And this is the judgment: the light came into the world, and people loved the darkness more than the light, because their deeds were evil.
For everyone who does evil hates the light, so that his deeds will not be exposed as evil.
But the one who practices the truth comes to the light, so that his deeds may be revealed as having been done in God.
After these things, Jesus and his disciples went into the land of Judea, and he stayed there with them and baptized.
John was also baptizing at Aenon near Salim, because there was plenty of water there, and people were coming and being baptized.
For John had not yet been thrown into prison.
Then a dispute arose between John's disciples and a Jew about purification.

They came to John and said to him, ‘Rabbi, the one who was with you on the other side of the Jordan, the one you testified about—look, he is baptizing and making many disciples, and everyone is coming to him.’
John answered, ‘A person cannot receive anything on his own unless it is given to him from heaven.’
You yourselves testify that I said, “I am not the Christ, but I was sent ahead of him.”
The one who has the bride is the bridegroom. But the bridegroom's friend, who stands and listens to him, rejoices greatly at the bridegroom's voice. So this joy of mine is now complete.
He must become greater, and I must become less.
The one who came from heaven is above everyone. The one who is from the earth belongs to the earth and speaks from the earth.
But the one who came from heaven testifies to what he has seen and heard, and no one accepts his testimony.
But the one who has accepted his testimony has certified that God is true.
For the one whom God sent speaks God's words, for God does not give the Spirit by measure.
The Father loves the Son and has placed everything in his hand.
Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life. But whoever does not believe in the Son will not see life; instead, God's anger will remain upon him.
So when the Lord learned that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was making and baptizing more disciples than John,
although it was not Jesus himself who was baptizing, but his disciples,
He left Judea and went back to Galilee.
he had to pass through Samaria.
So he came to a town in Samaria named Sychar, near the field that Jacob had given to his son Joseph.
Jacob's spring was there. Jesus, tired from walking along the road, sat down just as he was beside the spring. It was the sixth hour.
A woman came from Samaria to draw water. Jesus said to her, “Give me a drink.”
For his disciples had gone into the town to buy themselves something to eat.
The Samaritan woman said to him, “You are a Jew. How can you ask me for a drink when I am a Samaritan woman?” For Jews do not associate with Samaritans.
Jesus answered her, “If you knew God's gift and who it is who says to you, ‘Give me a drink,’ you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water.”
The woman said to him, “Sir, you have no bucket, and the well is deep. Where, then, do you get the living water?
Are you greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well and drank from it himself, along with his children and his livestock?”
Jesus answered her, “Everyone who drinks this water will be thirsty again.
But whoever drinks the water that I will give him will never be thirsty. Instead, the water that I will give him will become within him a spring of water welling up to eternal life.”
The woman said to him, “Sir, give me this water so that I will not come out here to draw water.”
He said to her, “Go, call your husband, and come here.”
The woman answered, saying, “I have no husband.” Jesus said to her, “You were right to say, ‘I have no husband.’”
“For you have had five husbands, and the man you have now is not your husband. What you have said is true.”
The woman said to him, “Sir, I see that you are a prophet.
Our ancestors worshiped on this mountain, but you say that the place where people must worship is in Jerusalem.”
Jesus said to her, “Believe me, woman, a time is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.
You worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, because salvation comes from the Jews.
But a time is coming, and it is now, when worshipers will indeed worship the Father in spirit and truth. For the Father seeks people like these to worship him.
God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship him in spirit and truth.”
The woman said to him, “We know that the Messiah is coming, the one called the Christ. When he comes, he will tell us everything.”
Jesus said to her, “I am he, the one speaking to you.”
At that moment his disciples came, and they were surprised that he was speaking with a woman. Yet no one said, “What are you looking for?” or “Why are you speaking with her?”
The woman left her water jar and went into the city. She said to the people,
"Come and see a man who told me everything I have done. Could this be the Christ?"
So they were coming out of the city and going to him.
Meanwhile, his disciples urged him, saying, "Rabbi, eat."
But he said to them, "I have food to eat that you do not know about."
So his disciples said to one another, "Has someone brought him something to eat?"
Jesus said to them, "My food is to do the will of the one who sent me and to finish his work.
Don't you say, 'There are still four months before the harvest comes'? Look, I tell you, lift up your eyes and look at the fields: they are already white, ready to be harvested.
The one who reaps will receive wages and gather fruit for eternal life, so that the one who sows and the one who reaps may rejoice together.
For in this the saying is true: 'One sows and another reaps.'
I sent you to reap what you had not worked for. Others did the hard work, and you have entered into their labor."
Many Samaritans from that city believed in him because of the woman's testimony: "He told me everything I have done."
So when the Samaritans came to him, they urged him to stay with them, and he stayed there for two days.
And many more believed his word.
They said to the woman, “We no longer believe because of what you said, for we have heard him ourselves, and we know that he truly is the Savior of the world.”
After the two days, he left that place for Galilee.
For Jesus himself had testified that a prophet has no honor in his own town.
When he came to Galilee, the Galileans welcomed him, having seen everything he had done in Jerusalem at the festival, for they too had gone to the festival.
He came again to Cana in Galilee, where he had turned the water into wine. There was a royal official whose son was sick in Capernaum.
When this man heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee, he went to him and begged him to come down and heal his son, for he was about to die.
Jesus then said to him, "Unless you see signs and wonders, you will not believe."
The royal official said to him, "Lord, come down before my son dies."
Jesus said to him, "Go; your son is alive." The man believed the word Jesus had spoken to him and went.
While he was going down, his servants met him and told him, "Your son is alive."
So he asked them at what time his son had begun to recover. They said, "The fever left him yesterday at the seventh hour."
The father realized that this was the very time when Jesus had said to him, "Your son is alive." And he believed, along with his entire household.
This was the second sign Jesus performed after coming from Judea to Galilee.
After this there was a Jewish festival, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
Now in Jerusalem, near the Sheep Gate, there was a pool called Bethsaida in Hebrew, with five covered walkways.
Under these lay a crowd of sick people: the lame, the blind, and those with withered bodies.
There was a man there who had been ill for thirty-eight years.
When Jesus saw him lying there and knew that he had been there a long time, he said to him, “Do you want to get well?”
The sick man answered him, “Lord, I have no one to put me down into the pool when the water is stirred up. While I am on my way, someone else goes down before me.”
Jesus said to him, “Get up, pick up your mat, and walk.”
Immediately the man became well, picked up his mat, and walked. Now that day was the Sabbath.
So the Jews said to the man who had recovered, “It is the Sabbath, and you are not allowed to carry your mat.”
He answered them, “The one who healed me is the one who told me, ‘Pick up your mat and walk.’”
They asked him, “Who is the man who told you, ‘Pick it up and walk’?”
But the man who had recovered did not know who he was, because Jesus had slipped away, as there was a crowd in that place.
After this Jesus found him in the temple and said to him, “Look, you are well. Do not sin again, so that something worse than this does not happen to you.”
The man went away and told the Jews, “Jesus is the one who healed me.”
Because of this, the Jews were persecuting Jesus, because he was doing these things on the Sabbath.
But Jesus answered them, “My Father is working right up to now, and I too am working.”
Because of this, the Jews tried even harder to kill him, because he was not only breaking the Sabbath but also saying, “God is my Father,” making himself equal to God.
So Jesus answered them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, the Son can do nothing on his own unless he sees the Father doing it. For whatever the Father will do, the Son will also do in the same way.
For the Father loves the Son and shows him everything he himself does. And he will show him greater works than these, so that you will be amazed.
For just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so the Son will also give life to those he wants.
For the Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son,
so that everyone may honor the Son just as they honor the Father. Whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent him.
Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever hears my word and believes the one who sent me has eternal life and does not come into judgment, but has passed from death into life.
Truly, truly, I tell you, a time is coming, and is now here, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live.
For just as the Father has life in himself, so he has also granted the Son to have life in himself.
And he gave him authority to carry out judgment, because he is the Son of Man.
And do not be amazed at this, because an hour is coming when everyone in the tombs will hear his voice
and come out: those who have done good to a resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to a resurrection of judgment.
I can do nothing on my own. I judge according to what I hear, and my judgment is just, because I do not seek my own will but the will of the one who sent me.
If I testify about myself, my testimony is not true.
There is another who testifies about me, and I know that the testimony he gives about me is true.
You sent to John, and he testified to the truth.
But I do not receive testimony from a human being. Rather, I say these things so that you may be saved.
He was the lamp that burned and gave light, and you were willing to rejoice in his light for a while.
But I have testimony greater than John's. For the works my Father gave me to complete—the very works I am doing—testify about me that the Father sent me.
And the Father who sent me has himself testified about me. You have never heard his voice or seen his form.
And you do not have his word remaining in you, because you do not believe in the one he sent.
Search the Scriptures, because you yourselves say that you have eternal life in them, and they are the ones that testify about me.
And you are unwilling to come to me so that you may receive life.
I do not receive honor from human beings.
But I know you: you do not have the love of God in you.
I have come in my Father's name, and you have not accepted me. If someone else comes in his own name, you will accept him.
How can you believe when you receive honor from one another and do not seek the honor that comes from the only One?
Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father. There is one who will accuse you: Moses, in whom you place your hope.
For if you believed Moses, you would believe me, because he wrote about me.
But if you do not believe his writings, how will you believe my words?
After these things, Jesus went to the other side of the Sea of Galilee, the Sea of Tiberias.
A large crowd was following him because they saw the signs he was performing on those who were sick.
Then Jesus went up the mountain and sat there with his disciples.
Now the Passover, the Jewish festival, was approaching.
Then Jesus looked up and saw that a large crowd was coming toward him. He said to Philip, “Where will we buy bread for these people to eat?”
He said this to test him, for he himself knew what he was going to do.
Philip answered him, “A hundred staters’ worth of bread would not be enough for each of them to receive a little.”
One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, said to him:
“There is a young boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish, but what will these do for such a crowd?”
Jesus said to them, “Have the people sit down.” There was plenty of grass in that place. So the men sat down, about five thousand of them.
Then Jesus took the loaves, gave thanks, and gave them to those who were reclining. Likewise, they received some of the fish.
When they had eaten their fill, he said to his disciples, “Gather up the pieces left over, so that nothing is lost.”
So they gathered them up and filled twelve baskets with pieces from the five barley loaves that were left over by those who had eaten.
When the people saw the sign he had performed, they said, “This really is the prophet who is coming into the world.”
When Jesus realized that they were coming to seize him and make him king, he withdrew again up the mountain by himself.
When evening came, his disciples went down to the sea.
They got into the boat to cross to the other shore of the sea, to Capernaum. It had become dark, and Jesus had not yet come to them.
A strong wind was blowing, and the sea grew rough.
When they had rowed about twenty-five or thirty stadia, they saw Jesus walking on the sea and approaching the boat, and they were afraid.
But he said to them, “It is I. Do not be afraid.”
Then they wanted to take him into the boat, and immediately the boat reached the shore where they were going.

The next day, the crowd standing on the other shore of the sea saw that there was no boat there except the one Jesus’ disciples had boarded, and that Jesus had not boarded the boat with his disciples, but his disciples had gone away alone.
And look, other boats came from Tiberias, near the place where they had eaten the bread after the Lord had given thanks over it.
When the crowd saw that neither Jesus nor his disciples were there, they themselves boarded the boats and came to Capernaum, looking for Jesus.
When they found him on the other shore of the sea, they said to him, “Rabbi, when did you come here?”
Jesus answered them, saying, “Truly, truly, I tell you, you are looking for me not because you saw signs, but because you ate the loaves and had your fill.
Do not work for the food that perishes, but rather for the food that lasts for eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you. For he is the one on whom God the Father has set his seal.”
Then they said to him, “What must we do to carry out the works of God?”
Jesus answered and said to them, “This is the work of God: that you believe in the one he sent.”
They said to him, “Then what sign do you perform, so that we may see and believe in you? What work do you do?
Our ancestors ate the manna in the wilderness, as it is written: ‘He gave them bread from heaven to eat.’”
Then Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, it was not Moses who gave you the bread from heaven, but my Father gives you the true bread from heaven.”
For the bread is the Son of God, who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.
Then they said to him, “Lord, give us this bread always.”
Then Jesus said to them, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will not be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty.
But I told you that you have seen me, and you do not believe.
Everyone my Father gives me will come to me, and I will not turn away anyone who comes to me.
For I came down from heaven not to do my own will, but the will of the one who sent me.
This is the will of the one who sent me: that I should lose none of all those he has given me, but raise them up on the last day.
For this is my Father's will: that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him should receive eternal life, and I will raise that person up on the last day.
Then the Jews were grumbling about him because he had said, "I am the bread that came down from heaven."
They were saying, “Is this not Jesus, Joseph’s son, whose father and mother we know? How, then, does he say, ‘I came from heaven’?”
Jesus answered them, "Do not grumble among yourselves.
No one can come to me unless my Father who sent me draws that person, and I myself will raise that person up on the last day.
It is written in the prophets, 'They will all be teachers [?] God.' Everyone who has heard from my Father and learned comes to me.
Not that anyone has seen the Father except the one who is from God; he is the one who has seen the Father.
Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever believes in me has eternal life.
I am the bread of life.
Your ancestors ate the manna in the wilderness, and they died.
But this is the bread that comes from heaven, so that anyone who eats of it will not die.
I am the living bread that came down from heaven. If anyone eats this bread, that person will live forever. The bread that I will give is my flesh, for the life of the world."
Then the Jews were arguing among themselves, saying, "How can this man give us his flesh to eat?"
Then Jesus said to them, "Truly, truly, I tell you, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you have no life in you.
Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise that person up on the last day.
For my flesh is true food, and my blood is true drink.
Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood will remain in me, and I in that person.
Just as the living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father, so whoever eats me will also live because of me.
This is the bread that came down from heaven, not like what the ancestors ate and then died. Whoever eats this bread will live forever."
He said these things in the synagogue while teaching in Capernaum.
Then many of his disciples, when they heard this, said, “This teaching is hard. Who can listen to it?”
But Jesus, knowing within himself that his disciples were grumbling about him, said to them, "Does this cause you to stumble?
Then what if you see the Son of Man going up to where he was before?
It is the Spirit who gives life; the flesh is of no use at all. The words I have spoken to you are spirit and life.
But some of you do not believe.” For Jesus knew from the beginning who did not believe and who would betray him.
And he said, “That is why I told you that no one can come to me unless it is granted to them by the Father.”
Because of this, many of his disciples turned back and stopped walking with him.
Then Jesus said to the Twelve, “Do you also want to leave?”
Simon Peter answered him, “Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life.
And we have believed and understood that you are the Christ, the Holy One of God.”
Jesus answered them, “Did I not choose you, the Twelve? Yet one of you is a devil.”
He was speaking about Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, for he was the one who would betray him, though he was one of the Twelve.
After this, Jesus traveled around Galilee. He did not want to travel around Judea because the Jews were seeking to kill him.
Now the Jewish Festival of Shelters was approaching.
So his brothers said to him, “Leave this place and go up to Judea so that your disciples too can see the works you are doing.
For no one does things in secret while seeking to be known publicly. If you do these things, show yourself to the world.”
For even his brothers did not believe in him.
Then Jesus said to them, “My time has not yet come, but your time is always ready.
The world cannot hate you, but it hates me because I testify about it that its deeds are evil.
You go up to the festival. I am not yet going to this festival because my time has not yet fully come.”
After saying these things, he stayed in Galilee.
But when his brothers had gone up to the festival, he too went up, not openly but in secret.
The Jews were looking for him in the temple and saying, “Where is he?”
There was much murmuring about him among the crowds. Some said, “He is a good man.” Others said, “No, he is misleading the crowd.”
Yet no one spoke openly about him because they were afraid of the Jews.
Halfway through the festival, Jesus went up to the temple and taught.
The Jews were amazed and said, “How is this man so learned without having been taught?”
Jesus answered them, saying, “My teaching is not mine but belongs to the one who sent me.
If anyone wants to do his will, they will understand whether this teaching comes from God or whether I am speaking on my own authority.
Someone who speaks on their own authority seeks their own glory. But someone who seeks the glory of the one who sent them is truthful, and there is no wrongdoing in them.
Wasn't it Moses who gave you the law? Yet none of you keeps the law. Why are you trying to kill me?
The crowd answered, “You have a demon! Who is trying to kill you?”
Jesus answered them, “I did one deed, and you are all amazed.
For this reason Moses gave you circumcision—not that it comes from Moses, but from the ancestors—and you circumcise a man on the Sabbath.
If a person receives circumcision on the Sabbath so that the law of Moses will not be broken, why are you angry with me because I made a whole person well on the Sabbath?
Do not judge with partiality, but judge fairly.”
Then some of the people of Jerusalem were saying, “Isn't this the man they are trying to kill?
Look, he is speaking openly, and they say nothing to him. Could the rulers and the chief priests really have recognized that he is the Christ?
But we know where this man comes from. When the Christ comes, no one will know where he comes from.”
Then Jesus called out as he taught in the temple, saying, “You know me, and you know where I come from. Yet I have not come on my own. The one who sent me is true, and you do not know him.
I know him because I am with him, and he is the one who sent me.”
Then they were trying to arrest him, but no one laid a hand on him, because his hour had not yet come.
Many in the crowd believed in him and were saying, “When the Christ comes, will he perform more signs than this man has performed?”
Then the Pharisees heard the crowd murmuring these things about him, and the chief priests and the Pharisees sent officers to arrest him.
Then Jesus said, “I am with you for a little while longer, and I will go to the one who sent me.
You will look for me and will not find me, and you cannot come where I am.”
Then the Jews said to one another, “Where will this man go that we will not find him? Will he go to those scattered among the Greeks and teach [?]?
What does he mean by saying, ‘You will look for me and will not find me, and you cannot come where I am’?”
On the last, great day of the festival, Jesus stood and called out, saying, “Let anyone who is thirsty come to me and drink.
Whoever believes in me, as Scripture has said, rivers of living water will flow from within him.”
He said this about the Spirit, whom those who believed in him were going to receive. For they had not yet received the Spirit, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.
Then some in the crowd, when they heard these words, were saying, “This really is the Prophet.”
Others were saying, “This is the Christ.” But some were saying, “Does the Christ come from Galilee?
Hasn't Scripture said that the Christ comes from David's descendants and from Bethlehem, the village where David lived?”
So a division arose in the crowd because of him.
Some of them wanted to arrest him, but no one laid a hand on him.
Then the officers went to the chief priests and the Pharisees, who said to them, “Why did you not bring him?”
The officers answered, “No one has ever spoken like this man.”
The Pharisees answered them, “Have you also been led astray?”
“Has any of the rulers or the Pharisees believed in him?”
“But this crowd, which does not know the law, is under a curse.”
Nicodemus, who had come to Jesus earlier and was one of them, said to them:
“Does our law judge a person without first hearing him and finding out what he is doing?”
They answered him, “Are you also from Galilee? Search the Scriptures, and you will see that the prophet will not arise from Galilee.”
Then Jesus spoke to them again, saying, “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness but will receive the light of life.”
The Pharisees therefore said to him, “You are testifying about yourself. Your testimony is not true.”
Jesus answered them, “Even if I testify about myself, my testimony is true, because I know where I came from and where I am going. But you do not know where I came from or where I am going.”
“You judge according to the flesh. I judge no one.”
“But even if I judge, my judgment is true, because I am not alone: I am with the Father who sent me.”
“It is also written in your law that the testimony of two people is true.”
“I testify about myself, and the Father who sent me also testifies about me.”
Then they said to him, “Where is your Father?” Jesus answered them, “You know neither me nor my Father. If you knew me, you would also know my Father.”
He spoke these words in the treasury while teaching in the temple. No one arrested him, because his hour had not yet come.
Then Jesus said to them again, “I am going away, and you will look for me, and you will die in your sin. Where I am going, you cannot come.”
Then the Jews said, “Is he going to kill himself, since he says, ‘Where I am going, you cannot come’?”
He said to them, “You are from the earth; I am from heaven. You are from this world; I am not from this world.”
“That is why I told you that you will die in your sins. For unless you believe that I am he, you will die in your sins.”
Then they said to him, “Who are you?” Jesus said to them, “I have been speaking to you from the beginning.”
“I have much to say about you and much to judge. But the one who sent me is true, and what I have heard from him is what I tell the world.”
They did not understand that he was speaking to them about the Father.
Then Jesus said to them, “When you lift up the Son of Man, then you will understand that I am he and that I do nothing on my own. Instead, I speak these things just as my Father taught me.”
And the one who sent me is with me, and he has not left me alone, because I always do what pleases him.
As he said these things, many believed in him.
So Jesus said to the Jews who had believed in him, “If you remain in the word, you are truly my disciples.
And you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.”
They answered him, “We are Abraham’s descendants, and we have never been slaves to anyone. How can you say, ‘You will become free’?”
Jesus answered them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, everyone who commits sin is a slave to sin.
The slave will not remain in the household forever, but the son will remain forever.
So if the Son sets you free, you will truly be free.
I know that you are Abraham’s descendants, but you are seeking to kill me because my word does not dwell in you.
I speak of what I have seen with my Father. So you too, do what you have seen with your father.”
They answered him, “Our father is Abraham.” Jesus said to them, “If you were Abraham’s children, you would do Abraham’s deeds.
But now you are seeking to kill me, a man who tells you the truth that he heard from God. Abraham did not do this.
You are doing your father’s deeds.” So they said to him, “We were not born from sexual immorality. We have only one Father, God.”
So Jesus said to them, “If God were your Father, you would love me, because I came and am coming from God. I did not come on my own, but he sent me.
Why do you not understand what I say? Because you cannot listen to my word.

You come from your father, the devil, and you want to carry out your father’s desires. He was a murderer from the beginning, and he did not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. Whenever the liar speaks, he speaks from what is his own, because he is a liar, and so is his father.
But because I tell the truth, you do not believe me.
Which of you can convict me of sin? If I tell the truth, why do you not believe me?
Whoever comes from God listens to God’s words. This is why you do not listen: you do not come from God.”
The Jews answered him, “Are we not right to say that you are a Samaritan and that you have a demon?”
Jesus answered, “I do not have a demon, but I honor my Father, and you dishonor me.
I do not seek my own glory. There is someone who will seek it and judge.
Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever keeps my word will never see death.”
So the Jews said to him, “Now we know that you have a demon. Abraham died, and so did the prophets, yet you say, ‘Whoever keeps my word will never taste death.’
Are you greater than our father Abraham, who died? The prophets also died. Who do you make yourself out to be?”
Jesus answered, “If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing. It is my Father who glorifies me, the one you say is your God.”
“You have not known him, but I know him. If I said, ‘I do not know him,’ I would be a liar like you. But I know him and keep his word.”
“Your father Abraham rejoiced that he would see my day. He saw it and was glad.”
Then the Jews said to him, “You are not yet fifty years old, and Abraham has seen you?”
Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, before Abraham came into being, I am.”
Then they picked up stones to throw at him, but Jesus hid himself and left the temple.
As he was passing by, he saw a man who had been blind from birth.
His disciples asked him, “Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, so that he was born blind?”
Jesus answered, “Neither this man nor his parents sinned. Rather, this happened so that God's works might be revealed in him.”
“We must do the works of the one who sent me while it is day. Night is coming, when no one will be able to work.”
“As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.”
After saying this, he spat on the ground, made mud with the saliva, and smeared the mud on the man's eyes.
He said to him, “Go and wash your face in the pool of Siloam,” which means “the one who was sent.” So he went, washed his face, and came back able to see.
Then his neighbors and those who had previously seen him as a beggar said, “Isn't this the man who used to sit and ask for charity?”
Some said, “It is he.” Others said, “No, but he looks like him.” He himself kept saying, “I am the man.”
Then they said to him, “How, then, were your eyes opened?”
He answered, “The man called Jesus made mud and smeared it on my eyes. He said to me, ‘Go to Siloam and wash your face.’ So I went and washed my face, and I could see.”
They said to him, “Where is that man?” He said, “I do not know.”
They brought the man who had been blind before the Pharisees.
Now it was the Sabbath when Jesus made the mud and opened his eyes.
Then the Pharisees also asked him, “How did you come to see?” He said to them, “He put mud on my eyes, and I washed my face, and I could see.”
Some of the Pharisees said, “This man is not from God, because he does not keep the Sabbath.” But others said, “How can a sinful man perform signs like these?” And there was a division among them.
They said again to the man who had been blind, “What do you say about him, since he opened your eyes?” He said, “He is a prophet.”
The Jews did not believe that he had been blind and had gained his sight until they called the parents of the man who had gained his sight.
They asked them, “Is this your son, whom you say you gave birth to blind? How, then, can he see now?”
His parents answered them, “We know that this is our son and that he was born blind.”
“But we do not know how he can now see, nor do we know who opened his eyes. He is old enough to speak for himself.”
His parents said these things because they were afraid of the Jews. For the Jews had already agreed that anyone who acknowledged him as the Christ would be expelled from the synagogue.
That is why his parents said, “He is old enough; ask him.”
So they called the man who had been blind a second time and said to him, “Give glory to God. We know that this man is a sinner.”
He answered, “I do not know whether he is a sinner. One thing I do know: I was blind, and now I can see.”
Then they said to him, “What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?”
He answered them, “I have already told you, and you did not listen. Why do you want to hear it again? Do you also want to become his disciples?”
They insulted him, saying, “You are that man's disciple, but we are disciples of Moses.
We know that God spoke with Moses, but we do not know where this man comes from.”
The man answered them, “That is the amazing thing: you do not know where he comes from, yet he opened my eyes.
We know that God does not listen to sinners. But if someone worships God and does his will, he listens to that person.
Never has anyone heard of someone opening the eyes of a person born blind.
If this man were not from God, he could do nothing.”
They answered him, “You were born entirely in sin, and you are going to teach us?” And they threw him out.
Jesus heard that they had thrown him out, and when he found him, he said to him, “Do you believe in the Son of Man?”
He said, “Lord, who is he, so that I may believe in him?”
Jesus said to him, “You have seen him, and the one speaking with you is he.”
“I came into this world for judgment, so that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind.”
Some of the Pharisees who were with him heard this and said to him, “Are we also blind?”
Jesus said to them, “If you were blind, you would have no sin. But now you say, ‘We see,’ so your sin remains.
Truly, truly, I tell you, anyone who does not enter the sheepfold through the gate but climbs in another way is a thief and a robber.
But the one who enters through the gate is the shepherd of the sheep.
The gatekeeper opens for him, and the sheep listen to his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
When he has brought out all his own sheep, he walks ahead of them, and the sheep follow him because they know his voice.
They will not follow a stranger, but will run away from him because they do not know the voice of strangers.”
Jesus told them this figure of speech, but they did not understand what he was saying to them.
Then Jesus said to them again, “Truly, truly, I tell you, I am the shepherd of the sheep.”
All who came are thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not listen to them.
I am the gate. If anyone enters through me, he will be saved. He will go in and come out and find pasture.
The thief comes only to steal, slaughter, and destroy. I came so that they might receive life and have it in abundance.
I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for his sheep.
But the hired worker, who is not a shepherd and does not own the sheep, sees the wolf coming, leaves the sheep, and runs away. The wolf snatches them and scatters them.
This is because he is a hired worker and does not care about the sheep.
I am the good shepherd. I know my own, and my own know me.
Just as the Father knows me, I too know the Father, and I will lay down my life for my sheep.
I also have other sheep that are not from this fold. I must gather them too. They will listen to my voice, and they will become one fold with one shepherd.
This is why my Father loves me: because I will lay down my life so that I may take it up again.
No one takes it from me. Rather, I lay it down of my own accord. I have the authority to lay it down, and I also have the authority to take it up. I received this command from my Father.
A division arose again among the Jews because of these words.
Many of them were saying, “He has a demon and is out of his mind. Why do you listen to him?”
Others said, “These are not the words of someone possessed by a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?”
At that time the Feast of Dedication took place in Jerusalem. It was winter.
Jesus was walking in the temple under Solomon’s portico.
Then the Jews gathered around him and said to him, “How long will you keep us in suspense? If you are the Christ, tell us plainly.”
Jesus answered them, “I told you, and you do not believe. The works I do in my Father’s name testify about me.”
But you do not believe because you are not among my sheep.
My sheep listen to my voice, and I know them, and they will follow me.
And I will give them eternal life. They will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand.
My Father, who gave them to me, is greater than everyone, and no one can snatch them out of my Father’s hand.
My Father and I are one.
The Jews picked up stones again to throw at him.
Jesus answered them, “I have shown you many good works from my Father. For which of these works are you stoning me?”
The Jews answered him, “We are not going to stone you for a good work, but for blasphemy, because you, a human being, make yourself God.”
Jesus answered them, “Is it not written in your law, ‘I said, you are gods’?”
If those to whom the word of God came were called gods—and Scripture cannot be set aside—
then do you say to the one whom the Father made holy and sent into the world, ‘You are blaspheming,’ because I said, ‘I am the Son of God’?
If I do not do my Father's works, do not believe in me.
But if I do them, even if you do not believe in me, believe the works, so that you may understand and know that the Father is in me and I am in the Father.
Then they tried again to seize him, but he escaped from their hands.
He went again to the other side of the Jordan, to the place where John had been baptizing at first, and he stayed there.
Many people went to him and said, “John performed no sign, but everything John said about this man is true.” And many believed in him there.
Now a man named Lazarus was sick. He was from Bethany, the village of Mary and her sister Martha.
This was the Mary who anointed the Lord with perfume and wiped his feet with her hair. Her brother Lazarus was sick.
So his sisters sent word to him, saying, "Lord, look, the one you love is sick."
When Jesus heard this, he said, "This sickness will not lead to death, but it is for God's glory, so that his Son may be glorified through it."
Now Jesus loved Martha, her sister Mary, and Lazarus.
So when he heard that Lazarus was sick, he stayed two days in the place where he was.
After that, he said to his disciples, "Let us go to Judea again."
The disciples said to him, "Rabbi, the Jews were just trying to stone you, and are you going there again?"
Jesus answered, "Are there not twelve hours in the day? If someone walks during the day, he does not stumble, because he sees the light of this world.
If someone walks at night, he stumbles, because the light is not in him."
He said these things, and afterward he told them, "Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I will go to wake him."
Then the disciples said to him, "Lord, if he has fallen asleep, he will get up."
Jesus had spoken about his death, but they thought he was speaking about sleep as rest.
Then Jesus told them plainly, "Lazarus has died.
And for your sake I am glad that I was not there, so that you may believe. But let us go to him."
Thomas, who was called Didymus, said to his fellow disciples, "Let us go too, so that we may die with him."
When Jesus arrived, he found that Lazarus had been in the tomb for four days.
Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia away.
Many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary to comfort them about their brother.
When Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went out to meet him, while Mary remained seated in the house.
Then Martha said to Jesus, "Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died."
But even now I know that whatever you ask [?] God, God will give you.
Jesus said to her, “Your brother will rise again.”
Martha said to him, “I know that he will rise again in the resurrection on the last day.”
Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me will live, even if he dies.
And everyone who lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?”
She said to him, “Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God, who is coming into the world.”
After saying this, she went and called her sister Mary, telling her privately, “The teacher has come and is calling for you.”
When she heard this, she quickly got up and went out to him.
Jesus had not yet entered the village but was still at the place where Martha had met him.
When the Jews who were in the house with her, comforting her, saw Mary get up quickly and go out, they followed her, saying, “She is going out to the tomb to weep there.”
When Mary came out to the place where Jesus was, she threw herself at his feet and said to him, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.”
When Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her also weeping, he was troubled in spirit like someone who is angry.
He said, “Where have you laid him?” They said to him, “Lord, come and see.”
Jesus wept.
Then the Jews said, “Look how he loves him!”
But some of them said, “Could this man, who opened the blind man’s eyes, not also have kept this man from dying?”
Then Jesus, again angry within himself, came to the tomb. It was a cave, with a stone over its entrance.
Jesus said, “Take that stone away.” Martha, the dead man’s sister, said to him, “Lord, he already smells, for this is his fourth day.”
Jesus said to her, “Did I not tell you that if you believe, you will see the glory of God?”
Then they removed the stone from there. Jesus lifted his eyes toward heaven and said, “My Father, I thank you because you have heard me.”
I knew that you always hear me, but I said this because of the crowd standing here, so that they would believe that you are the one who sent me.”
After saying this, he shouted in a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!”
The man who had died came out, his feet and hands bound with strips of cloth and his face wrapped in a cloth. Jesus said to them, “Untie him and let him go.”
Many of the Jews who had come to Mary, when they saw what he had done, believed in him.
But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.
Then the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered the council and said, “What are we going to do? This man is performing many signs.”
If we let him continue like this, everyone will believe in him, and the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation.
But one of them, Caiaphas, who was high priest that year, said to them, “You know nothing.
Nor do you consider that it is better for us for one man to die for the people than for the whole nation to perish.”
He did not say this on his own, but as high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus would die for the nation,
and not for the nation alone, but also to gather the scattered children of God together in one place.
So from that day on, they made plans to kill him.
Jesus therefore no longer went about openly among the Jews. Instead, he left that place for the region near the wilderness, to a town called Ephraim, and stayed there with his disciples.
The Jewish Passover was approaching, and many people went up to Jerusalem from the countryside before the Passover to purify themselves.
They were looking for Jesus and said to one another as they stood in the temple, “What do you think? Will he not come to the festival?”
The chief priests and the Pharisees had given an order that if anyone knew where he was, they should tell them so that they could arrest him.
Six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, whom Jesus had raised from the dead.
They prepared a dinner for him there. Martha served, and Lazarus was one of those reclining at the table with him.
Then Mary took a pound of very expensive perfume made from pure nard, anointed Jesus’ feet, and wiped his feet with the hair of her head. The house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume.
Judas Iscariot, one of his disciples, who was going to betray him, said,
“Why was this perfume not sold for three hundred staters and the money given to the poor?”
He said this not because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief. He had charge of the money box and used to steal what was put into it.
Then Jesus said, “Leave her alone, so that she may keep it for the day of my burial.
For the poor are always with you, but I am not always with you.”
A large crowd of Jews learned that he was there. They came not only because of Jesus, but also to see Lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead.
But the chief priests made plans to kill Lazarus too,
because many Jews were going away because of him and believing in Jesus.
The next day, a large crowd of those who had come to the festival heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem.
They took palm branches and went out to meet him, shouting, “Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord, the King of Israel!”
Jesus found a donkey and mounted it, just as it is written,
“Do not be afraid, daughter of Zion. Look, your king is coming to you, sitting on a donkey’s colt.”

His disciples did not understand these things at first. But when Jesus was glorified, they remembered that these things had been written about him and that these were the things they had done for him.
The crowd that was with him testified that he had called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him from the dead.
This was also why the crowd went out to meet him: they had heard that he had performed this sign.
Then the Pharisees said to one another, “You see that you are accomplishing nothing. Look, the world has gone after him.”
Now there were some Greeks among those who were going up to worship at the festival.
They approached Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, and asked him, “Sir, we want to see Jesus.”
Philip went and told Andrew, and Andrew and Philip told Jesus.
Jesus answered them, “The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.”
“Truly, truly, I tell you, unless a grain of wheat falls to the ground and dies, it remains alone. But if it dies, it produces much fruit.”
“Whoever loves his life will lose it, and whoever hates his life in this world will find it for eternal life.”
“If anyone is going to serve me, let him follow me. Where I am, my servant will also be there. If anyone serves me, my Father will honor him.”
“Now my soul is troubled. And what shall I say? ‘My Father, save me from this hour’? But this is why I have come to this hour.”
“My Father, glorify your name.” Then a voice came from heaven: “I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again.”
The crowd standing there and listening said, “That was thunder.” Others said, “An angel spoke to him.”
Jesus answered, “This voice did not come for my sake, but for yours.”
“Now is the judgment of this world. Now the ruler of this world will be thrown down.”
“And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw everyone to myself.”
He said this to indicate what kind of death he would die.
Then the crowd answered him, “We have heard from the law that the Christ will remain forever. How can you say that the Son of Man must be lifted up?”

Then Jesus said to them, “The light is with you for a little while longer. Walk while you have the light, so that darkness does not overtake you. Whoever walks in darkness does not know where he is going.”
“While you have the light, believe in the light, so that you may become children of the light.” Jesus said these things, then went away and hid from them.
Although he had performed all these signs before them, they did not believe in him.
So that the words spoken by Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled: “Lord, who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?”
For this reason they could not believe, because Isaiah also said:
“For he has closed their eyes and closed their hearts, so that they may not see with their eyes or understand with their hearts and turn back, and I would heal them.”
Isaiah said these things because he saw the glory of God and spoke about him.
Nevertheless, many of the rulers also believed in him. But because of the Pharisees, they did not acknowledge it, so that they would not be expelled from the synagogue.
For they loved praise from people more than praise from God.
Jesus cried out, “Whoever believes in me does not believe in me, but in the one who sent me.”
“And whoever sees me sees the one who sent me.”
“I am the light who has come into the world, so that everyone who believes in me will not remain in darkness.”
And if anyone hears my words and keeps them, I do not judge him, for I did not come to judge the world, but to save it.
The one who rejects me and does not accept my words has someone who judges him: the word I have spoken is what will judge him on the last day.
For I have not spoken on my own authority, but my Father who sent me has himself given me a command about what to say and what to speak.
And I know that his command is eternal life. So whatever I say, I say just as my Father told me.
Before the Passover festival, Jesus knew that his hour had come to leave this world and go to the Father. Having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them to the end.
And when supper took place, the devil had already put it into the heart of Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, to betray him.
Jesus knew that the Father had placed everything in his hands, and that he had come from God and was going to God.
He rose from supper, laid aside his clothes, took a towel, and tied it around himself.
And he poured water into the basin and began to wash the disciples’ feet and wipe them with the towel tied around him.
Then he came to Simon Peter, who said to him, “Lord, are you going to wash my feet?”
Jesus answered him, “You do not understand what I am doing now, but afterward you will understand it.”
Peter said to him, “I will never let you wash my feet.” Jesus answered him, “If I do not wash your feet, you have no share with me.”
Simon Peter said to him, “Lord, not only my feet, but wash my hands and my head too!”
Jesus said to him, “Someone who has bathed needs only to wash his feet; otherwise he is completely clean. You too are clean, but not all of you.”
For he knew who would betray him. That is why he said, “Not all of you are clean.”
Then, when he had finished washing his feet, he took his clothes, reclined again, and said to them, “Do you understand what I have done for you?”
“You call me Teacher and Lord, and you are right to say so, for that is what I am.”
“So if I, the Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you too ought to wash one another’s feet.”
“For I have given you an example, so that you too should do just as I have done for you.”
“Truly, truly, I tell you, no slave is greater than his master, nor is any messenger greater than the one who sent him.”
“If you know these things, you are blessed if you do them.”
“I am not speaking about all of you. I know those I have chosen. But this is so that the Scripture may be fulfilled: ‘The one who eats my bread has lifted his heel against me.’”
“I am telling you now, before it happens, so that when it happens you may believe that I am he.”
“Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever receives the one I send receives me, and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me.”
When Jesus had said these things, he became troubled in spirit and testified, saying, “Truly, truly, I tell you, one of you will betray me.”
Then the disciples looked at one another, puzzled about whom he was speaking.
One of his disciples, whom Jesus loved, was reclining against Jesus’ chest.
Simon Peter therefore motioned to him to ask who Jesus was talking about.
So he leaned back against Jesus’ chest and said to him, “Lord, who is it?”
Jesus answered, “It is the one to whom I will give the bread after dipping it.” After dipping the bread, he gave it to Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot.
After he took the bread, Satan entered him. Jesus then said to him, “What you are going to do, do quickly.”
But none of those reclining at the table understood why he said this to him.
For some thought that, because Judas had charge of the money box, Jesus had told him, “Buy what we need for the festival,” or that [?] should give something to the poor.
So after taking the bread, he immediately went out. It was night.
When he had gone out, Jesus said, “Now the Son of Man has been glorified, and God has been glorified in him.
If God has been glorified in him, God will also glorify him in himself, and he will glorify him immediately.
My children, I am with you for only a little longer. You will look for me, and just as I told the Jews, ‘You cannot come where I am going,’ I now tell you the same.
But I give you a new commandment: love one another. Just as I have loved you, you too must love one another.
By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.”
Simon Peter said to him, “Lord, where are you going?” Jesus answered him, “You cannot follow me now where I am going, but you will follow me afterward.”
Peter said to him, “Lord, why can I not follow you now? I will lay down my life for you.”
Jesus answered him, “Will you lay down your life for me? Truly, truly, I tell you, a rooster will not crow until you have denied me three times.
Do not let your hearts be troubled. Believe in God, and believe in me.
There are many places to live in my Father’s house. If that were not so, I would have told you, for I am going to prepare a place for you.
And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and take you to myself, so that you too may be where I am.
And you know the way to the place where I am going.”
Thomas said to him, “Lord, we do not know where you are going. How can we know the way?”
Jesus said to him, “I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.
If you have known me, you will know my Father too. From now on you know him and have seen him.”
Philip said to him, “Lord, show us your Father, and that will be enough for us.”
Jesus said to him, “I have been with you all this time, and you have not known me, Philip? Whoever has seen me has seen the Father. How can you say, ‘Show us your Father’?
Do you not believe that I am in my Father and my Father is in me? The words I say to you, I do not say on my own. Rather, my Father who lives in me does his works.
Believe me that I am in my Father and my Father is in me. If not, believe his works.
Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever believes in me will also do the works I do, and will do greater works than these, because I am going to my Father.
And whatever you ask in my name, I will do, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
If you ask for anything in my name, I will do it.
If you love me, you will keep my commandments.
And I too will ask the Father, and he will give you another Advocate, so that he may be with you forever.
The Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive because it neither sees him nor knows him. You know him, because he will stay with you and be in you.
I will not leave you as orphans. I am coming to you.
In a little while, the world will no longer see me, but you will see me. Because I live, you too will live.
On that day you will understand that I am in my Father, and you are in me, and I am in you.
Whoever has my commandments and keeps them is the one who loves me. My Father will love the one who loves me, and I too will love him and reveal myself to him.
Judas the Canaanite said to him, “Lord, why will you reveal yourself to us and not reveal yourself to the world?”
Jesus answered him, “If someone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him. We will come to him and make our home with him.”
“Whoever does not love me will not keep my word. And the word you hear is not mine, but belongs to my Father who sent me.”
“I have told you these things while I am with you.”
“But when the Advocate comes, the Holy Spirit whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you everything and remind you of every word I have said to you.”
“I leave you peace. I give you my own peace. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your heart be troubled or grow weak.”
“You heard me tell you, ‘I will go away and come back to you.’ If you loved me, you would rejoice that I am going to the Father, because my Father is greater than I am.”
“And now I have told you before it happens, so that when it happens, you may believe.”
“I will not speak much more with you, because the ruler of this world is coming, and he has no hold on me.”
“But so that the world may know that I love my Father, I do just as he commanded me. Get up; let us leave this place.”
“I am the true vine, and my Father is the gardener.”
“Every branch in me that does not bear fruit, he will remove. And every branch that bears fruit, he will prune so that it may bear more fruit.”
“You are already clean because of the word I have spoken to you.”
“Remain in me, and I in you. Just as a branch cannot bear fruit on its own unless it remains in the vine, neither can you unless you remain in me.”
“I am the vine; you are the branches. Whoever remains in me, and I in him, will bear much fruit, because without me you can do nothing.”
“If someone does not remain in me, he is thrown out like a branch and dries up. They will gather the branches, throw them into the fire, and burn them.”
“If you remain in me and my words remain in you, ask for whatever you want, and it will be done for you.”
My Father is glorified in this: that you bear much fruit and become my disciples.
Just as my Father has loved me, I too have loved you. Remain in my love.
If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love, just as I have kept my Father's commandments and remain in his love.
I have told you these things so that my joy may be in you and your joy may be complete.
This is my commandment: that you love one another just as I have loved you.
No one has greater love than this: to lay down his life for his friends. You are my friends
if you do what I command you.
I will no longer call you my slaves, because a slave does not know what his master is doing. But I have called you my friends, because I have made known to you everything I heard from my Father.
You did not choose me, but I chose you and appointed you so that you would go and bear fruit, and your fruit would last forever, so that if you ask the Father in my name, he will give it to you.
I command you these things so that you love one another.
If the world hates you, know that it hated me before you.
If you belonged to the world, the world would love what is its own. But because you do not belong to the world, and I chose you out of the world, the world hates you.
Remember the words I told you: 'No slave is greater than his master.' If they persecuted me, they will persecute you. If they kept my word, they will also keep yours.
But they will do all these things to you because of my name, because they do not know the one who sent me.
If I had not come and spoken to them, they would have no sin. But now they have no excuse for their sin.
Whoever hates me also hates my Father.
If I had not done among them the works that no one else had done, they would have no sin. But now they have seen me and have hated both me and my Father.
But this is so that the words written in their law may be fulfilled: 'They hated me without cause.'
When the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from the Father—the Spirit of truth, who comes from the Father—he will testify about me.
And you too testify, because you have been with me from the beginning.
I have told you these things so that you will not fall away.
They have expelled you from the synagogue. But a time is coming when everyone who kills you will think he is offering service to God.
And they will do these things to you because they have known neither my Father nor me.
I have told you these things so that when their time comes, you will remember that I told you about them. I did not tell you these things from the beginning because I was with you.
But now I am going to the one who sent me, and none of you asks me, 'Where are you going?'
But because I have told you these things, sorrow has filled your hearts.
But I am telling you the truth: it is better for you that I go away. For if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you. But if I go, I will send him to you.
And when he comes, he will convict the world concerning sin, righteousness, and judgment.
Concerning sin, because they do not believe in me.
Concerning righteousness, because I am going to the Father, and you will no longer see me.
Concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world has been condemned.
I still have many things to tell you, but you cannot bear them now.
When he comes, the Spirit of truth, he will guide you in all truth. For he will not speak on his own, but he will say what he hears, and he will tell you what is going to happen.
He is the one who will glorify me, because he will take what is mine and tell it to you.
In a little while you will stop seeing me, and again, in a little while you will see me again.
Some of his disciples said to one another, “What is this that he is telling us: ‘In a little while you will not see me, and again, in a little while you will see me,’ and ‘I am going to the Father’?”
And they said, “What, then, is this ‘little while’? We do not know what he is saying.”

Jesus knew that they wanted to question him. He said to them, “Are you asking one another about this, because I said, ‘In a little while you will stop seeing me, and in a little while you will see me again’?
Truly, truly, I tell you: you will weep and mourn, but the world will rejoice. You will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will turn into joy.

When a woman is about to give birth, she has sorrow because her hour has come. But when she has given birth to the child, she no longer remembers the distress, because of the joy that she has brought a human being into the world.
So you too have sorrow now, but afterward I will see you again, and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take your joy away from you.
On that day you will not question me about anything. Truly, truly, I tell you: whatever you ask the Father for, he will give you in my name.
Until now you have asked for nothing in my name. Ask, and you will receive, so that your joy may be complete.
I have told you these things in figures of speech. An hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you in figures of speech, but will speak to you plainly about the Father.
On that day you will ask in my name, and I am not telling you that I will plead with the Father on your behalf.
For the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me and have believed that I come from the Father.
I came from the Father and came into the world. Now I will leave the world again and go to the Father.”
The disciples said to him, “Look, now you are speaking plainly and are not using any figure of speech.
Now we understand that you know everything and do not need anyone to question you. Because of this, we believe that you came from God.”
Jesus answered them, “Do you now believe?”
Look, an hour is coming, and it has come, when you will be scattered, each to his own place, and you will leave me alone. Yet I am not alone, because my Father is with me.
I have told you these things so that you may have peace in me. You have trouble in the world, but take courage: I have overcome the world. Jesus said these things.
Jesus said these things and lifted his eyes to heaven, saying, “My Father, the hour has come. Glorify your Son so that your Son may glorify you.
Just as you gave him authority over all humanity, let him give eternal life to everyone you have given him.
And this is eternal life: that they know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom you sent.
I have glorified you on earth because I have completed the work you gave me to do.
So now, my Father, glorify me in your presence with the glory I had with you before the world came into being.
I have revealed your name to the people you gave me out of the world. They were yours, and you gave them to me, and they have kept your word.
Now I have understood that everyone you have given me comes from you.
For I have given them the words you gave me, and they truly accepted them—that I came from you—and they believed that you sent me.
I pray for them. I do not pray for the world, but for those you have given me, because they are yours.
Everything that is mine is yours, and what is yours is mine, and I have been glorified in them.
I am no longer in the world, but I am coming to you. My holy Father, protect them in your name, which you gave me, so that they may be one, just as we are.
While I was with them, I protected them in your name, which you gave me. I guarded them, and none of them was lost except the son of destruction, so that the Scripture would be fulfilled.
But now I am coming to you, and I say these things in the world so that they may have my joy fulfilled within them.
I have given them your word, and the world has hated them because they do not belong to the world, just as I do not belong to the world.
I do not ask you to take them out of the world, but to protect them from the evil one.
They do not belong to the evil one, just as I do not belong to the world.
Purify them in the truth. Your word is the truth.
Just as you sent me into the world, I too have sent them into the world.
And I purify myself for their sake, so that they too may be purified in the truth.
I am not praying for these alone, but also for the others who will believe in me through their word.
So that they may all be one, just as you, my Father, are in me and I am in you; so that they too may be in us, so that the world may believe that you sent me.
And I have given them the glory you gave me, so that they may be one, just as we are one.

I am in them, and you are in me, so that they may be in me, made completely one, and so that the world may understand that you are the one who sent me and that you have loved them just as you have loved me.
My Father, I want those you have given me to be with me where I am, so that they may see my glory, which you gave me because you loved me before the foundation of the world.
My righteous Father, the world has not known you, but I have known you, and these people have recognized me as the one you sent.
And I have made your name known to them, and I will make it known again, so that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I myself may also be in them.
After Jesus said these things, he went out with his disciples to the other side of the Kidron stream, where there was a tree. He and his disciples went into that place.
Judas, who was going to betray him, also knew that place, because Jesus had often gathered there with his disciples.
So Judas took a company of soldiers and some officers from the chief priests and the Pharisees, and came to that place with lanterns, torches, and weapons.
Jesus, knowing everything that was coming upon him, went out and said to them, “Who are you looking for?”
They answered him, “We are looking for Jesus of Nazareth.” Jesus said to them, “I am he.” Judas, who had betrayed him, was also standing with them.
When Jesus said to them, “I am he,” they moved backward and fell to the ground.
Again he asked them, “Who are you looking for?” They said, “Jesus of Nazareth.”
Jesus answered them, “I told you that I am he. So if you are looking for me, let these people go.”
This was so that the words he had spoken might be fulfilled: “Of those you gave me, I have not lost anyone.”
Simon Peter had a sword. He drew it, struck the high priest’s slave, and cut off his right ear. The slave’s name was Malchus.
Jesus said to Peter, “Put your sword into its sheath. Shall I not drink the cup that my Father has given me?”
Then the company of soldiers, their commander, and the Jewish officers seized Jesus and bound him.
They brought him to Annas first, because he was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.
Caiaphas was the one who had advised the Jews that it was better for one person to die for the people.
Simon Peter and the other disciple were following Jesus. That disciple was known to the high priest, and he went with Jesus into the high priest’s courtyard.
But Peter was standing outside at the door. The disciple who was known to the high priest went out, spoke to the woman guarding the door, and brought Peter inside.
The slave woman guarding the door said to Peter, “You are not also one of this man’s disciples, are you?” He said, “No.”
The slaves and officers were standing there, having lit a charcoal fire, and were warming themselves because it was cold outside. Peter was also standing there, warming himself.
The high priest questioned Jesus about his disciples and his teaching.
Jesus answered him, “I have spoken openly to the world. I have always taught in the synagogues and in the temple, where all the Jews gather, and I have said nothing in secret.
Why are you questioning me? Ask those who heard what I said to them. They know what I said.”
When he said these things, one of the officers standing there slapped Jesus, saying, “Is this how you answer the high priest?”
